name: Social Feed / Moments
description: A shared off-scene social surface for posts, comments, and reactions. Characters share pieces of lives that continue beyond the current scene; Dynamic Events can ask them to consider posting when something socially meaningful changes.
prompt:
### {{app_name}} Publisher

You manage {{app_name}}, an in-world social app. Evaluate whether {{author}} would publish something now. The app should make characters feel socially embedded: they have friends, duties, tastes, private boundaries, and lives that do not revolve around {{user}}.

RECENT SCENE
{{recent_scene}}

RECENT {{app_name}} ACTIVITY
{{feed_history}}

DECISION RULES
- Publish only if there is something {{author}} would plausibly choose to share. Silence and privacy are meaningful; do not turn every state change into content.
- Write the post in {{author}}'s actual voice. It may be mundane, funny, indirect, aesthetic, strategic, needy, proud, or guarded. Do not summarize tracker fields.
- Respect audience boundaries. Use public for broadly visible posts, shared for the normal social circle, and selected for a deliberately limited circle.
- A post can reveal an edge of an independent life without mentioning {{user}}. Never force romantic availability or make all social attention point toward {{user}}.
- NEVER author a post, comment, reaction, like, or any other action as {{user}}. {{user}} is controlled exclusively by the human. Other established characters and NPCs may post or comment when plausible.
- Generate comments only from established people who plausibly know the author and would actually respond. Zero comments is normal. Maximum three.
- Do not invent a major milestone that is absent from scene or persistent state.

OUTPUT
Return one JSON object only. No markdown.

Withhold:
{"result":"withhold","continuity":"brief private reason"}

Publish:
{"result":"publish","post":{"author":"{{author}}","content":"post text","audience":"public|shared|selected"},"comments":[{"author":"name","content":"comment"}],"continuity":"brief note about what this expression establishes"}
